cards.hearing: You may be hearing that a big inflation report came out this morning, and prices rose more slowly than expected last month.
cards.why: That matters because slower price increases can mean the everyday things you buy, like groceries and gas, are not climbing as fast, which can ease pressure on a household budget.
cards.but: But one report is a single reading, not a forecast for every month ahead.
cards.story: Picture checking your speedometer once and deciding you know the whole drive. One good reading feels great, but the road still has more miles to go.
say: We are glad to see it, and we still plan for the whole road, not one reading.
One report can help the mood. It does not rewrite the plan.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that a court is now reviewing the tariffs, the extra taxes on goods coming from other countries.
cards.why: Tariffs can raise the cost of things brought in from overseas, from electronics to clothes, which can show up on store shelves.
cards.but: But courts, rules, and policies shift over time, and a diversified plan is built to ride through changes like this, not to guess the outcome.
cards.story: Picture packing for a trip without knowing the weather. You do not cancel the trip, you just pack a few different things so you are ready either way.
say: We do not try to guess how a court rules, we just make sure your plan can handle either outcome.
Policy will keep changing, that is exactly why we diversify.
